root_idea.summary: The root centers on cleaving or splitting, especially by cutting through a constricted part such as the throat; it extends to slaughter, opening vessels, channels cut through earth, and related derivatives.
root_idea.development: The basic notion of cleaving develops into throat-cutting slaughter and sacrificial killing, while related Classical usages apply the idea to piercing or opening a vessel, cuts and cracks, and channels that cleave the ground.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form ذَبَحَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form ذَبَّحَ.
Displayed as the nominal citation form ذِبْحٌ.

senses.definition: To slaughter an animal by cutting its throat; to sacrifice it.
senses.usage_conditions: The central Quranic use concerns slaughtering an animal, including slaughter for food or sacrifice. Active, passive, and inflected forms are included under this citation form.

senses.definition: To kill or slay, by extension from slaughter.
senses.usage_conditions: An extended use can apply to a person or other living being and need not specify the technical procedure of animal slaughter.

senses.definition: To slaughter or kill repeatedly, in succession, or in large numbers.
senses.usage_conditions: The Form II use is explicitly associated with many victims or repeated slaughter; in the Quran it describes the systematic slaughtering of sons.

senses.definition: A sacrificial victim: an animal prepared for slaughter or one that has been slaughtered.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence denotes a sacrificial victim supplied as a ransom; the noun can refer either to the intended victim or to the completed sacrifice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave, split, slit, or rip open; specifically, to open a musk follicle or broach a vessel to draw out its contents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are non-Quranic extensions of the cleaving notion and include opening by cutting or piercing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render lawful or allowable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extension associated with slaughter making animal flesh lawful as food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To choke or obstruct the breath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of weeping or another thing that constricts the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect severely or distress through thirst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used specifically with thirst as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a beard, to flow down beneath the chin so that the front of the area under the jaw becomes visible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use concerning the growth or fall of the beard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lower the head while inclining the body in prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported usage, attributed to some authorities but disputed by another authority, who regarded the form as a mistake for دبَّحَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To slaughter or slay one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal Form VI usage; the associated saying about mutual praise is a figurative application of this meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or prepare a slaughtered animal for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form VIII usage concerning obtaining a prepared slaughtered or sacrificed animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal sacrificed to the jinn as an offering intended to avert harm or ill luck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A culturally specific sacrificial practice, distinct from the Quranic ransom context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A red edible plant, including a plant whose root or stem yields a sweet edible substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective plant name with variant descriptions in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of white truffle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal plant or fungus designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode or manner of slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or manner noun referring to the procedure of slaughter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease, ulcer, or obstructive swelling in the throat that can choke and kill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also be used figuratively for an inwardly harmful condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A poisonous plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant is described as poisonous to those who eat it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quick or sudden death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression موتٌ ذُبَاحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cleft, slit, or ripped open.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or passive-participial use corresponding to the non-slaughter cleaving branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slaughtered or sacrificed; a slaughtered animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may be applied substantivally and may agree with animals of different grammatical gender and number.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fit, proper, destined, or prepared to be slaughtered as a sacrifice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This describes the intended sacrificial victim before the slaughter has necessarily been carried out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slain man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended substantival use for a human victim.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person whose occupation or habitual work is slaughtering; an executioner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The occupational sense includes the later use for an executioner.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cracks or cuts in the inner sides or sole of the foot, especially near the toes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily-condition noun with plural ذَبَابِيحُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a pair of bright stars in Capricorn, one appearing to threaten a nearby small star as though about to slaughter it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional astronomical name for one of the lunar mansions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mark made with a hot iron across the throat, or the instrument used to make it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized object noun derived from the slaughtering action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hair growing between the area beneath the lower jaw and the throat area used for slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical or descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal allowable or suitable for slaughter, including camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes eligibility for slaughter rather than the completed act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where slaughter is performed, including the throat region that serves as the site of slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote either a physical place or the anatomical slaughtering site.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The chancel or altar area of a church, where offerings are made.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the place of sacrifice; its plural is مَذَابِحُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trench or channel in the earth, including a small torrent channel that cleaves the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical use for a natural or water-cut channel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A knife or other instrument used to perform slaughter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The instrument need not be a knife if it serves the same slaughtering function.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clean or pure and not requiring slaughter, as applied to things in the sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended usage treating such things as already exempt from the need for slaughter.
